clinician.trajectory_summary: An 86-year-old male presented with worsening chronic lower back and right lower extremity pain, numbness, and ambulatory dysfunction. MRI lumbar spine revealed acute insufficiency fractures in the sacrum and a suspicious metastatic lesion in the L3 vertebral body, along with hydroureteronephrosis and a cystic focus in the iliacus muscle. Biopsy of the L3 lesion confirmed metastatic carcinoma consistent with urothelial carcinoma via immunohistochemical markers CK7, CK20, P40, Uroplakin, and Gata-3. Laboratory studies showed leukocytosis, anemia, acute kidney injury, and urinalysis with pyuria and microscopic hematuria. There was no reported prior history of urothelial carcinoma or bladder cancer, and no detailed neurological or abdominal/pelvic physical exam findings were documented. Treatment course and clinical outcomes were not reported.
